text: As 2025 approaches, marketers are looking to stay ahead of the curve. With new tech and changing consumer behavior, strategies like personalization, automation, and AI are evolving fast. It’s time to rethink your approach and get ready for what’s next. What is a Digital Strategy? A digital strategy is a plan that outlines how a business will use digital channels, technologies, and tools to achieve its goals. It focuses on driving growth, improving customer engagement, and maximizing online presence through tactics like SEO, social media, content marketing, and paid ads. A strong digital strategy aligns with overall business objectives and adapts to the evolving digital landscape. 10 Digital Marketing Strategies for 2025 1. Search Engine Optimization (SEO) – Maximizing organic visibility SEO, or Search Engine Optimization, is the practice of improving a website’s visibility on search engines by optimizing content, structure, and credibility. By using relevant keywords, enhancing user experience, and earning authoritative backlinks, businesses can attract organic traffic and connect with people searching for valuable information. Its primary goal is to attract high-intent organic traffic and build lasting brand authority by optimizing content for relevant searches, enhancing user experience, and earning trust through quality backlinks and consistent engagement. Types of SEO SEO includes various strategies that work together to improve your site’s visibility. These include: On-page SEO Optimizes content, keywords, meta tags, and headings to improve rankings. For example, using relevant keywords and a clear content structure in blog posts enhances visibility and makes it easier for search engines to understand your content. Off-page SEO Focuses on building site authority through external factors like backlinks. Earning quality backlinks from trusted websites through guest blogging or mentions boosts your site’s credibility and improves rankings on search engines. Local SEO Optimizes your site for location-based searches, which is essential for businesses with local customers. For example, a restaurant can optimize for “best Italian restaurant near me” and update its Google Business Profile to capture local search traffic. Technical SEO Improves backend elements such as page speed, schema markup, and Core Web Vitals to enhance crawlability and user experience. Optimizing your site’s code and images ensures faster loading times, especially for mobile users, improving overall site performance. Ecommerce SEO Tailors SEO efforts for online stores by optimizing product pages with structured data, detailed descriptions, and customer reviews. These strategies not only improve rankings but also boost conversions by making it easier for customers to find and trust products. Enterprise SEO Designed for large organizations with extensive content, enterprise SEO focuses on scalability through automation and comprehensive keyword strategies. This ensures that large volumes of content are efficiently optimized and targeted at broad, relevant search queries. To build a strong SEO strategy: Start with thorough keyword research using online tools to identify the terms your audience is searching for. Optimize your on-page elements by refining title tags, meta descriptions, headers, and content structure to ensure it aligns with user intent and engages your audience. Focus on off-page techniques like link building, guest blogging, and digital PR to develop a solid backlink profile, boosting your site’s authority. Regularly track your website’s performance and adjust your strategy based on the insights gathered, ensuring continuous improvement. Pro tip: Leverage content silos for SEO organization Create content silos by grouping related topics into distinct, well-structured sections on your website. This internal linking strategy not only helps search engines understand the relationships between topics but also improves the user experience, guiding visitors through relevant content more effectively. 2. Pay-per-click (PPC) advertising – High-impact paid marketing PPC advertising is a paid strategy that offers businesses instant visibility on search engines and social media platforms. Unlike organic growth, which takes time, PPC delivers quick exposure, capturing potential customers while complementing long-term marketing efforts. By bidding on specific keywords and audience segments, businesses ensure their ads appear at the top of search results, social media feeds, and partner websites, driving targeted traffic. Key elements of PPC advertising include: Search ads : Text-based ads that show up on search engine results pages. These are highly effective for attracting traffic when users search for relevant keywords. Display ads : Banners that appear on partner websites and video platforms like YouTube. Display ads increase brand awareness and help attract new audiences. Retargeting ads : Ads targeted at users who previously visited your website but didn’t convert. These ads encourage users to return and complete their purchase. Social media ads : Paid campaigns on platforms like Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and TikTok, utilizing detailed audience targeting based on demographics, interests, and behaviors. If you want to build a high-converting PPC strategy: Select a platform : Choose ad platforms that align with your target audience and business goals. For instance, B2B companies might find LinkedIn Ads more beneficial, while e-commerce brands may see greater success with Facebook and Google Ads. Create your ad : Write compelling ad copy with clear calls-to-action (CTAs). Make sure your ad creatives are visually engaging and resonate with your target audience. Optimize your landing page : Ensure consistency between your ad and landing page messaging. Optimize page load speed and design for conversion. A/B test different layouts and CTAs for better results. Measure & analyze : Regularly assess ad performance using analytics tools to track key metrics like click-through rates (CTR), cost per acquisition (CPA), and return on ad spend (ROAS). Pro tip: Use “Dayparting” to maximize ad performance. Dayparting is the strategy of scheduling ads to run only during specific times of the day or days of the week when your target audience is most likely to engage. By analyzing historical data, you can pinpoint peak times for conversions and adjust your campaign schedule to maximize your budget, ensuring your ads are only shown when they’re most likely to drive results. 3. Content marketing – Engaging & educating your audience Content marketing is all about creating and sharing valuable content to attract and keep the right audience. Done well, it helps businesses build trust, establish authority, engage customers, and improve search rankings. Take a software company, for example. By sharing blog posts on productivity tips, it shows expertise while subtly promoting its project management tool. Content marketing comes in many forms, each serving a unique purpose in engaging audiences and driving results. Common forms of content marketing include: Blog posts & SEO articles establish authority and boost search rankings by providing in-depth, educational content tailored to what people are searching for. Video content thrives on platforms like YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram Reels, using compelling visuals and storytelling to capture attention. Podcasts & webinars offer an immersive way to share expertise, build thought leadership, and connect with audiences through conversation. Infographics & data-driven content break down complex ideas into digestible, shareable visuals that enhance understanding. Ebooks & whitepapers dive deeper, serving as lead magnets in B2B marketing by offering valuable insights in exchange for contact information. To make content marketing truly effective, you will need a clear strategy. To create this, you’ll need to: Understand your audience’s pain points. You can use surveys and analytics to uncover their needs. Organize content with topic clusters and pillar pages to strengthen SEO and guide users through related information. Maximize reach by repurposing content. Turn blog posts into videos, infographics, or bite-sized social media content to engage different audiences. Pro tip: Focus on content velocity over perfection Instead of obsessing over making every piece of content perfect, focus on publishing consistently and refining based on performance. High-performing brands iterate quickly, using real-time data to optimize and improve rather than waiting for perfection. The faster you test and adjust, the more effective your content will become. 4. Social media marketing (SMM) – Growing brand awareness & engagement Social media marketing leverages platforms like Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, Twitter, and YouTube to create a vibrant, engaged community around your brand. The focus is on building meaningful connections, sharing engaging content, and driving conversations that boost your brand’s visibility and credibility. Here are some key social media strategies you can employ: Organic strategies : These involve creating content that naturally drives engagement and brand advocacy without the use of paid promotions. Paid advertising : These utilize targeted ads to reach specific audience segments and increase conversions. Influencer collaborations : These help expand your reach and build trust by partnering with industry-relevant influencers. Each social media platform has its own distinct audience and features, which should guide the type of content you create for each. For example: Facebook & Instagram are visually-driven platforms with a diverse audience, so use engaging visuals, retargeting, stories, and reels to foster engagement and maintain connections. LinkedIn caters to professionals, making it ideal for thought leadership and networking—share insightful articles, industry news, and valuable insights to establish credibility. TikTok & YouTube shorts thrive on quick, attention-grabbing content, so create dynamic, short videos that entertain and encourage sharing. Twitter (X) is built for real-time updates and conversations, so actively participate in discussions and engage directly with your audience to stay relevant. Pro tip: Harness the power of user-generated content (UGC) Encourage your followers to create and share content related to your brand by running campaigns or contests. Not only does UGC increase engagement, but it also builds trust and social proof, as people are more likely to trust content created by their peers. 5. Email marketing – High-ROI customer retention strategy Email marketing remains one of the most effective ways to nurture relationships, drive conversions, and boost customer loyalty. By delivering personalized and automated messages, you can stay top-of-mind with your audience and guide them seamlessly through their customer journey. Key email campaigns include: Welcome sequences , which introduce new subscribers to your brand’s value and set the tone for future interactions. Lead nurturing emails that provide helpful content to guide prospects through the sales funnel. Cart abandonment emails , which recover lost sales by gently reminding visitors of the items left behind. Re-engagement emails to re-activate inactive subscribers and keep them engaged with your brand. To create a high-performing email strategy: A/B test subject lines, content, and send times to optimize performance. Segment your audience based on behavior and demographics to deliver highly relevant, targeted content. Automate workflows to ensure your emails reach the right person at the right time, without the need for constant manual effort. Pro tip: Personalize beyond the basics Go beyond just using a subscriber’s first name in your emails. Leverage behavioral data—like past purchases or browsing history—to craft emails that feel deeply personal and highly relevant, increasing engagement and conversions. 6. Marketing automation & AI-powered personalization – Scaling marketing efficiency Marketing automation, combined with AI-powered personalization, allows you to scale your efforts and deliver tailored experiences at every touchpoint. Automating repetitive tasks not only saves time but ensures that each customer interaction feels relevant and timely, driving both efficiency and effectiveness. Key areas of implementation include: Email automation that delivers timely messages, such as cart recovery emails or personalized content recommendations. AI-driven chatbots that provide instant support and engagement, helping customers anytime they need it. Dynamic content personalization that adjusts website content, emails, and ads based on individual user behavior in real-time. Lead scoring & predictive analytics , which help prioritize leads by predicting their likelihood to convert. Social media scheduling to keep a consistent online presence without manual effort. To execute an effective strategy: Identify tasks that can be automated and choose tools that align with your needs. Build streamlined workflows that guide users through their journey, ensuring a personalized experience at every stage. Pro tip: Automate feedback loops for continuous improvement Set up automated requests for customer feedback at crucial moments, like after a purchase or interaction with support. AI can analyze this feedback to identify trends and insights, allowing you to continually refine your marketing efforts and improve customer satisfaction. 7. Influencer & affiliate marketing – Leveraging trust for higher conversions Influencer and affiliate marketing rely on high-profile bloggers and social media personalities to promote your brand, using the trust they’ve built with their audience to drive engagement and conversions. Influencer marketing involves collaborating with social media figures to showcase your brand across posts, stories, reels, and videos. This strategy significantly boosts brand awareness and credibility, which leads to higher conversion rates. For example, a lifestyle influencer featuring your eco-friendly product line can drive high-quality traffic and sales. However, working with top-tier influencers can be expensive, so it’s important to align these partnerships with your budget and strategic goals. Affiliate marketing is a performance-based model where affiliates earn commissions only when they drive actual sales. This cost-efficient strategy allows affiliates to promote your brand across various platforms and methods, ensuring that you pay only for conversions. How to maximize influencer & affiliate marketing: Start by defining clear objectives, whether you want to increase brand awareness, generate leads, or drive direct sales. Select influencers and affiliates whose audiences align with your brand and track performance using robust analytics and affiliate dashboards. Offering exclusive incentives, like discounts, can help drive even higher conversions. Pro tip: Use micro-influencers with hyper-niche audiences Instead of relying solely on big-name influencers, consider working with micro-influencers who have smaller, highly engaged audiences in a specific niche. Their recommendations often feel more personal and trustworthy, leading to higher engagement and conversion rates. 8. Video marketing – The most engaging content format Video marketing is the strategic use of video content to engage audiences, convey your brand message, and drive conversions. With platforms like YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram dominating the digital space, video has emerged as the most captivating format for content consumption. Types of video content include: Short-form videos on platforms like TikTok and Instagram Reels are perfect for quick, engaging content. Long-form educational content such as tutorials, reviews, or webinars that establish authority and provide in-depth insights. Live streaming & webinars offer real-time engagement, fostering direct interaction with your audience. Product demos & explainer videos that highlight your product’s features and benefits, guiding customers through their purchasing decision. To maximize video marketing: Choose the video format that aligns with your campaign objectives. Optimize videos with SEO-friendly titles, descriptions, and tags. Repurpose longer content into bite-sized clips for different platforms. Test thumbnails and video titles through A/B testing to find what drives the most engagement. Pro Tip: Use interactive video features to drive engagement Add interactive elements like clickable CTAs, polls, and quizzes within your videos. This keeps viewers engaged longer and encourages them to take immediate action, such as signing up or making a purchase. 9. Voice search optimization & AI assistants – Preparing for the future of search Voice search optimization is the process of tailoring your content for voice-activated devices. As voice search grows in popularity, optimizing your content for natural, conversational language is crucial for capturing this rapidly expanding segment of search traffic. Effective tactics include: Incorporating conversational keywords, like long-tail, question-based phrases such as “What are the best digital marketing strategies?” Structuring content in an FAQ format, offering clear and concise answers that help voice assistants understand and deliver your content. Utilizing schema markup to add structured data to your site, enabling voice assistants to pull relevant answers directly from your content. Optimizing for local searches by updating your Google Business Profile, ensuring you appear in location-based “near me” queries. To stay ahead, consider developing an integrated audio content strategy, like launching podcasts or incorporating voice-overs into your content. Additionally, regularly test your content’s performance using feedback from voice assistants to improve your visibility. Pro Tip: Focus on featured snippets Voice assistants often pull answers directly from featured snippets in search results. Structure your content to answer questions in a concise, clear format to increase your chances of being featured in these snippets and enhance your visibility in voice search results. 10. Web design & UX optimization – enhancing user experience for higher conversions Web design and UX optimization are all about creating a visually appealing, easy-to-navigate website that drives engagement and conversions. By focusing on intuitive design and seamless user experiences, you can keep visitors on your site longer and turn them into loyal customers. To optimize web design and UX: Adopt a mobile-first design and prioritize fast load speeds to ensure optimal performance across all devices. Use tools like Google Lighthouse to assess and improve your site’s speed and performance. Simplify navigation by creating a clear, intuitive structure that allows users to easily find what they need. Use high-impact CTAs and minimalistic forms to encourage quick responses and reduce friction for visitors. Ensure accessibility by following ADA standards to make sure your website is usable by all users, regardless of their abilities. Continuously refine your design. Conduct A/B testing to identify the best-performing layouts, CTAs, and design elements. Use AI-powered heatmaps to analyze user behavior and implement real-time assistance, like chatbots, to address customer queries promptly. Pro Tip: Use Micro-Interactions for Engagement Incorporate small, engaging animations or micro-interactions, such as button hover effects or form field animations. These subtle details improve the user experience, making your site feel more interactive and enhancing overall satisfaction, which can increase conversion rates. How to Build an Effective Digital Marketing Strategy Step 1: Set SMART goals Start by defining SMART goals , which should be Specific , Measurable , Achievable , Relevant , and Time-bound . This approach ensures your marketing strategy aligns with business growth and drives measurable results. Focus on both short-term and long-term objectives that evolve over time. Best practices include: Set short-term goals (3-6 months) to drive immediate results. Set long-term goals (12+ months) to support sustained business growth. Align KPIs with business objectives, such as sales revenue or lead conversion. Pro Tip Regularly review your goals and adjust them based on ongoing performance to stay aligned with changing business needs and market trends. Step 2: Research & define your target audience Next, research and define your target audience. Creating detailed buyer personas is crucial. Focus on: Demographics : Age, location, income level, education Psychographics : Interests, values, lifestyle, online behavior Pain points : Challenges your product/service can solve Gather insights through audience research and feedback to understand their needs and refine your approach. Analyze how they interact with your website and content to enhance user experience. Step 3: Conduct a competitive analysis Once you’ve defined your audience, it’s time to conduct a competitive analysis. Analyze competitors’ strategies to uncover gaps and opportunities. Key focus areas include: SEO : Keyword rankings, backlink profiles Content marketing : High-performing blog posts, engagement rates Social media : Engagement rates, follower growth PPC campaigns : Successful ad strategies, offers This analysis will help you identify areas where your brand can offer unique value and stand out in the market. Pro Tip Reverse-engineer your competitors’ successful strategies by studying their ad copies, offers, and engagement trends. This allows you to refine your approach, providing a unique value proposition where they may be lacking. Step 4: Audit existing digital channels & assets Before launching new strategies, review your current digital assets to ensure they’re optimized for success. Conducting an audit helps identify gaps and areas for improvement. Best practices include: Performing an SEO audit to check page load speed, mobile responsiveness, and fix broken links. Addressing indexing issues and ensuring proper structured data implementation. Evaluating content performance using metrics like engagement rates, bounce rates, and conversions. Reviewing email lists and social media to identify areas for improvement. Pro Tip Use AI-powered tools to refresh outdated blog posts, improving their search rankings and boosting engagement. Step 5: Select the right digital marketing channels Choosing the right marketing channels depends on your audience, industry trends, and goals. Prioritizing the most effective channels maximizes ROI and helps you reach your target audience. Best practices include: Focusing on high-ROI channels like SEO, PPC, and email marketing. Using a multi-channel approach to avoid relying on a single platform. Combining organic and paid strategies to increase reach and visibility. Pro Tip Use cross-channel retargeting to reconnect with visitors who’ve interacted with your brand, encouraging them to convert and boosting brand awareness. Step 6: Develop & implement your strategy Once you’ve selected the right channels, it’s time to execute your strategy efficiently. A well-structured plan ensures all marketing efforts align with business goals and deliver consistent results—and partnering with a results-driven LA Marketing Agency can provide the local expertise and full-service support needed to execute and scale your strategy. Best practices include: Creating a 12-month roadmap to outline key milestones and objectives. Aligning content, social media, PPC, and email campaigns to maintain consistent messaging. Scheduling content in advance with automation tools to save time and stay organized. Pro Tip Leverage AI-driven marketing automation to personalize content and optimize campaigns based on real-time insights, making them more relevant and effective. Step 7: Optimize & automate marketing processes Marketing automation tools help businesses scale their efforts while delivering personalized experiences for customers. Automation allows you to streamline tasks and focus on more strategic aspects of your marketing. Best practices include: Using chatbots and AI-powered CRMs to nurture leads and improve customer interactions. Automating email sequences for better segmentation and retargeting. Implementing AI-driven predictive analytics to understand customer behavior and guide your marketing decisions. Pro Tip Use AI-powered personalization engines to boost engagement and conversions by providing tailored experiences for each customer. Step 8: Monitor, measure, and improve To ensure continuous growth and maximize ROI, track and optimize your marketing efforts regularly. This helps refine your strategy and ensures your campaigns stay effective. Best practices include: Running A/B tests to improve landing pages, ad copy, and CTAs. Tracking engagement and conversion rates to measure campaign success. Pro Tip Conduct monthly strategy reviews to stay aligned with business goals and make ongoing improvements for better results. Measuring Success: Digital Marketing Metrics & Analytics Measuring digital marketing success is critical to optimizing campaigns, refining strategies, and ensuring that marketing investments drive meaningful business results. Without proper tracking, businesses risk making decisions based on assumptions rather than real data. Digital analytics provides insights into customer behavior, engagement trends, and conversion performance, allowing businesses to refine their approach and achieve higher ROI. Here are some key reasons to track performance: Data-Driven Decisions : Use analytics to optimize marketing efforts based on real insights instead of guesswork. Maximizing ROI : Ensure that marketing spend translates into measurable revenue and engagement. Customer Insights : Gain a deeper understanding of audience behavior, preferences, and pain points to refine targeting and messaging strategies. Key digital marketing metrics & KPIs to track To measure the success of your digital marketing efforts and refine your strategy, it’s essential to track key performance metrics that provide insights into user behavior and website performance. 1. Website traffic Website traffic measures the number of visitors to your site and is an essential indicator of brand awareness and reach. Analyzing traffic sources (organic, paid, direct, referral, and social) helps businesses understand where their audience is coming from. Optimization tip: Segment traffic by source (Organic, Paid, Referral) to identify top-performing channels and refine your marketing strategies accordingly. 2. Bounce rate Bounce rate indicates the percentage of visitors who leave your website after viewing only one page. A high bounce rate may signal issues with site content, usability, or load speed. To fix the bounce rate, improve page speed, enhance content relevance, and optimize CTAs (Call-to-Actions) to encourage deeper engagement. 3. Average session duration & pages per session These metrics show how long users stay on your site and how many pages they visit per session. Longer sessions and higher page views indicate strong engagement and effective content strategies. Optimization tip: Use heatmaps (Hotjar, Crazy Egg) to analyze user behavior and identify opportunities for improving content flow and site navigation. Conversion Metrics (How Well You Turn Visitors into Leads/Sales) 4. Conversion rate (CVR) Conversion rate measures the percentage of visitors who take a desired action, such as filling out a form, subscribing to a newsletter, or completing a purchase. A high conversion rate indicates that your website effectively drives user engagement and actions. Fix: A/B test different CTAs, landing page layouts, and offers to identify what drives the highest conversions. 5. Customer acquisition cost (CAC) CAC measures the cost of acquiring a new customer, considering marketing spend across various channels. Lowering CAC improves profitability and efficiency. Optimization tip: Reduce CAC by enhancing organic reach through SEO, content marketing, and social media engagement. 6. Cart abandonment rate This metric tracks the percentage of users who add products to their cart but do not complete a purchase. High abandonment rates may indicate a complicated checkout process or unexpected costs. Fix: Simplify checkout, offer free shipping, and use retargeting emails to remind users to complete their purchase. Email marketing metrics (Assessing engagement & effectiveness) 7. Open rate The open rate measures the percentage of email recipients who open your emails. A low open rate can indicate weak subject lines or poor sender reputation. Fix: Optimize subject lines, test send times, and improve sender reputation. 8. Click-through rate (CTR) CTR measures the percentage of email recipients who click on links within your email. Higher CTRs indicate strong engagement and compelling content. Optimization tip: Use buttons instead of text links and place CTAs above the fold to increase engagement. Paid advertising & ROI metrics (Evaluating ad campaign performance) 9. Return on ad spend (ROAS) ROAS calculates the revenue earned per dollar spent on advertising campaigns, measuring the effectiveness of paid media. Optimization tip: Improve audience targeting, refine ad copy, and A/B test landing pages to boost performance. 10. Cost per click (CPC) & Cost per acquisition (CPA) CPC measures the cost of each click on an ad, while CPA calculates the cost to acquire a new customer through advertising. Fix: Use negative keywords, improve ad relevance scores, and enhance targeting precision to lower costs. Social media metrics (Measuring engagement & brand awareness) 11. Engagement rate Engagement rate measures interactions (likes, shares, comments, saves, and clicks) relative to reach or followers. Optimization tip: Post at peak engagement times and create interactive content like polls and Q&A sessions. 12. Follower growth rate This metric tracks the rate at which your social media audience is expanding over time. Fix: Leverage viral content formats (memes, challenges, user-generated content) to drive growth. Customer retention & lifetime value metrics (Long-term success indicators) 13. Customer lifetime value (LTV) LTV estimates the total revenue a business can expect from a single customer over their lifetime. Optimization tip: Improve customer loyalty through personalized experiences, rewards programs, and retention marketing. 14. Churn rate Churn rate measures the percentage of customers who stop engaging with or purchasing from a brand over a given period. Fix: Launch re-engagement campaigns, provide personalized offers, and ensure consistent follow-ups. By consistently monitoring and analyzing these digital marketing metrics, businesses can ensure that their strategies are aligned with their goals and continuously improve their performance to drive sustainable growth. 7 Common Digital Marketing Mistakes to Avoid Even the most well-planned digital marketing strategies can fail if businesses fall into common traps. Here are seven key mistakes that marketers should avoid to ensure long-term success. 1. Relying on intuition instead of analyzing real performance data Relying on gut feelings can lead to misguided decisions, especially when it comes to digital marketing. To make data-driven decisions, it’s crucial to regularly track key metrics like conversion rates, traffic sources, and ROI. How to fix it: Track essential metrics using tools like Google Analytics, GA4, and CRM systems. Conduct A/B testing on landing pages, emails, and ad campaigns to identify the highest-performing elements. Leverage AI-powered analytics to predict trends and optimize your campaigns automatically, ensuring better results over time. 2. Chasing quick wins without a long-term plan While viral posts and aggressive paid ads may provide short-term boosts, they don’t always contribute to sustainable growth. A strategy that focuses only on quick wins can leave your business vulnerable to market changes and fluctuations. How to fix it: Develop a comprehensive 12-month marketing roadmap with clear short- and long-term goals that guide your efforts. Invest in SEO, content marketing, and brand authority-building to drive consistent, organic growth. Balance paid advertising with organic strategies to reduce reliance on fluctuating ad spend and build a solid foundation for future success. 3. Using a one-size-fits-all approach in ads, emails, and content Treating all customers the same can lead to disengagement. Generic messaging doesn’t resonate with diverse audiences, and can miss opportunities for better connections and conversions. How to fix it: Segment your audience based on demographics, behavior, past interactions, and buying stage to ensure more relevant content. Leverage personalization tools and AI-driven recommendations to craft tailored experiences that drive engagement. Test different ad creatives and messaging for each customer segment to find what resonates best. 4. Neglecting mobile users, slow-loading websites, and complex navigation A slow website or poor mobile experience can cause frustration, leading to high bounce rates and missed opportunities. Ensuring a smooth experience across devices is crucial to keep users engaged. How to fix it: Ensure your website loads within 3 seconds using tools like Google PageSpeed Insights to improve user experience. Use responsive design so your website functions seamlessly on mobile devices. Implement heatmap tracking to better understand user behavior and identify pain points in navigation. 5. Only focusing on acquiring new customers instead of nurturing existing ones It’s easy to get caught up in attracting new customers, but overlooking your current customers can mean missed revenue opportunities from repeat business and brand loyalty. How to fix it: Set up retargeting ads to re-engage visitors who didn’t convert initially. Build loyalty programs and email sequences to retain customers and keep them coming back. Use post-purchase follow-ups, upselling, cross-selling tactics, and exclusive offers to further engage your existing customer base. 6. Prioritizing paid ads over organic search growth Paid ads may offer immediate results, but relying solely on them can lead to short-term gains without a lasting foundation. Investing in SEO can provide sustainable traffic and long-term value. How to fix it: Develop a keyword-driven content plan to improve long-term SEO rankings. Optimize for Google AI Overviews, featured snippets, and zero-click searches to capture more visibility. Regularly update blog posts, product descriptions, and website content to maintain relevance and improve search engine rankings. 7. Failing to leverage AI-powered tools, automation, and new trends Staying competitive means embracing new technologies and trends. AI and automation can save time and enhance marketing efficiency, but many businesses fail to capitalize on these tools. How to fix it: Automate repetitive tasks like email workflows, social media scheduling, and chatbot interactions to save time. Use AI-generated content tools, but maintain human oversight to ensure consistency with your brand’s voice. Stay ahead of trends like AI-driven SEO, voice search, and interactive content to ensure your marketing strategies remain cutting-edge. Conclusion As the digital marketing landscape evolves, success in 2025 demands a balanced approach that blends innovation with proven, data-driven strategies. You can build a comprehensive digital marketing strategy that drives measurable growth by embracing these top 10 strategies—from advanced SEO and PPC to innovative content, dynamic social media engagement, and personalized automation. text: 10 digital marketing strategy examples to inspire your next campaign Is your team investing in digital marketing? Following best practices certainly helps, but even then it can be tough to achieve digital marketing success. From social media and email to paid ads and SEO, there are dozens of digital marketing methods to choose from. This can make it difficult to know which channels will help you be successful. If you need creative inspiration, it’s best to learn from the brands that have come before you and done it well. In this guide, we’ll explore 10 examples of successful digital marketing strategies. We’ll explain why they were so successful, as well as how you can emulate these strategies in your own campaigns. After reading, you’ll have a better understanding of what digital marketing is, the different types of digital marketing and actionable strategies for improving your digital marketing performance. In this post, we’ll cover: What is digital marketing? Types of digital marketing Digital marketing strategy best practices Digital marketing strategy examples What is digital marketing? Digital marketing is the promotion of products and services through digital channels. If your business promotes itself through a screen, you’re engaging in digital marketing. Since the practice encompasses nearly any digital channel, there are several types of digital marketing. For example, you can do digital content marketing that uses guest blogs to build trust and expertise. Or you can do social media marketing with branded hashtags to build brand awareness and create user-generated content (UGC). Types of digital marketing Now that we have a clear understanding of what digital marketing is, let’s take a closer look at the different types. There are countless ways to do digital marketing, but these are some of the most common types: Social media marketing Search engine optimisation (SEO) Search engine marketing (SEM) SMS marketing Email marketing Content marketing Pay-per-click advertising (PPC) Over-the-top (OTT) streaming ads Most businesses use a combination of these digital strategies to create a unique marketing mix that best appeals to their target audience. Organic approaches like social media and SEO are more popular with small businesses, while enterprises tend to invest more in paid strategies like PPC. Digital marketing strategy best practices Before we can look at examples of digital marketing in action, it’s important to understand what makes a digital marketing strategy successful. Regardless of the business model or audience, all great marketing strategies follow these four best practices. 1. Know your audience Marketing doesn’t have a purpose without an audience. The goal of marketing is to engage with and convert leads into customers. If you fail to understand your audience’s wants and needs, your messaging and targeting will miss their mark. Knowing your audience helps you to meet your customers’ needs. Successful digital marketing teams collect data on their customers to inform their digital marketing strategies. You can learn more about your audience through analytics, customer surveys and feedback. From there, you can create buyer personas to model customer journeys based on what you know about your customers. Your marketing and sales teams rely on these profiles to create better, more focused content tailored specifically to your audience and their needs. Digital marketing is the promotion of products and services through digital channels. If your business promotes itself through a screen, you’re engaging in digital marketing. 2. Set goals Marketing campaigns lose focus without a goal. Since focus is the key to success, every successful marketing campaign starts with a goal. But generic goals like “increase sales” aren’t helpful. A $1 increase in sales technically counts as success, but that’s surely not your actual goal. This is why goals should be specific and measurable. The world’s best digital marketing campaigns set goals using the SMART goal-setting framework . Your goals need to be: Specific. The goal clearly describes what you want to accomplish. Measurable. This establishes a quantifiable metric that identifies when you’ve achieved your goal. Attainable. The goal is realistic, given the resources and time you have. Relevant. The goal aligns with your company’s priorities and will have a meaningful impact on your business. Time-bound. You aim to achieve the goal by a specific date. Under the SMART framework, generic goals like “increase sales” can become more actionable objectives like “increase gross profits by 15% by the end of Q2.” This makes it much easier to determine if a campaign was successful or not. It also gives you something tangible to aim for, which provides marketing teams more clarity. 3. Evaluate past efforts Digital marketing is always changing and that means digital campaigns are always a work in progress. However, brands can learn a lot about their marketing strategies when they analyse past performance. Before you plan new campaigns for the year, audit past campaigns. What did you do well? Where did you fall short? Were there any opportunities you wish you capitalised on? By looking at previous campaigns, you’ll learn how to design more effective campaigns going forward. Plus, evaluating your past efforts can also save you time and effort in the future. Sometimes you can repurpose assets, such as images and blog posts, from previous campaigns. 4.Consider logistics Finally, all successful digital marketing campaigns consider their resources and constraints. What are the logistics of executing a campaign? Many businesses over allocate or under allocate resources and both are mistakes that can hurt your return on investment (ROI). Always consider your: Budget. Marketing campaigns need to generate ROI. If you spend too much on a campaign that doesn’t generate enough revenue, it will put your marketing budget in the red. People. Have you got the staff to pull this off? Does your team have the expertise to execute your marketing strategy? Do you need to hire third-party vendors or contractors? These are all important questions to ask. Time. Time constraints will limit the scope of your digital marketing campaigns. Don’t overschedule your marketing team — find a balance that allows you to generate ROI without perennially tight deadlines. Channels. Which channels are you using to promote your business? Whether it’s social media, video, blogs or a podcast, the channels you choose will naturally come with limitations and rules. Marketers should shoot for the moon, but it’s still important to consider logistics that could limit your campaign. These important limitations will tell you what’s reasonable for your business to achieve, so you might need to adjust your SMART goals to accommodate them. Digital marketing strategy examples Now that we understand the basics of digital marketing strategy success, it’s helpful to see best practices in action. Learn from these 10 prominent examples of digital marketing strategy to design better campaigns going forward. 1. Apple #ShotoniPhone Apple used content marketing to convince more people to give its smartphone macro camera a try. The now-viral campaign showcased the power of the iPhone 13 Pro and iPhone 13 Pro Max cameras. Instead of generating branded content about its new, higher quality cameras, Apple let its users showcase this feature. The brand encouraged Apple customers to submit user-generated photos with the hashtags #ShotoniPhone and #iPhonemacrochallenge. Better yet, Apple turned this content marketing strategy into a contest. It selected 10 winning photos to feature on its social media, website, billboards and other marketing channels. Not only did this generate buzz for Apple’s macro camera, but it also helped the brand source user-generated content of its product in action. This gave the brand thousands of high-quality UGC images to pull from. 2. Nike Air VaporMax In another smart example of a content marketing strategy, Nike partnered with the YouTube channel “What’s Inside?” to promote its Nike Air VaporMax shoes. The YouTube channel, which dissects items to see what’s inside them, garnered more than 7 million views on this 10-minute video dedicated to Nike. “What’s Inside?” has 7.11 million subscribers on YouTube, which ensured millions of people would see the brand collaboration. By partnering with an established YouTube channel, Nike also leveraged popular influencers to promote its new line of shoes. 3. BuzzFeed email marketing BuzzFeed is known for viral listicles and clickable quizzes, but its email marketing strategies are also effective. Email is an often-overlooked strategy, but in an age when tracking cookies are going away, brands should use email to collect first-party data while engaging with their subscribers. BuzzFeed is unique because it offers a variety of different newsletters. Depending on their interests, subscribers can sign up for newsletters featuring recipes, travel tips, news, pop culture and even courses. BuzzFeed succeeds at email marketing not only because of its attention-grabbing content, but also because of its clarity. The brand is clear about email content and frequency, which gives subscribers more agency to control their inboxes. 4. Airbnb host guidebooks If you’ve ever booked an Airbnb, you might have noticed a guidebook attached to the booking confirmation page . These guidebooks are a form of content marketing and user-generated content created by Airbnb hosts. The guidebooks inform guests about restaurants, landmarks and things to do during their stay. While this is helpful to Airbnb renters, it also serves as a clever form of content marketing. Airbnb is improving the quality of renters’ stays with suggested activities and advice from locals. The better the quality of a renter’s stay, the more likely they are to share their experience with other travellers and re-book for another stay. 5. Myprotein brand ambassadors Health and fitness is a growing category. Myprotein is a nutrition and apparel company that was looking to increase its market share in this competitive industry. But the brand found that athletes were hesitant to try new, unproven protein brands. Myprotein used social media and affiliate marketing to persuade more athletes to try its products. It partnered with a handful of fitness influencers, including Bella Rahbek and Armando Nava, to promote exclusive bundles and savings to the influencers’ social media followings. Through coupon codes, hashtags and customised content, Myprotein boosted brand awareness and incentivised more social media shoppers to give their products a try. 6. Priceline pay-per-click ads Pay-per-click marketing costs can add up quickly, but this digital marketing strategy can net fast results for businesses. That’s something Priceline discovered when it ran a large PPC campaign in 2016. The travel brand reportedly spent more than $3 billion on PPC in 2016. Although most brands don’t have a $3 billion PPC budget, Priceline backed up its campaigns with a sound strategy. It used the power of paid ads to appear on relevant search engine results pages for competitive queries. It targeted keywords like “compare flight prices” and “cheap flights” to stand out. Priceline also highlighted costs and discount bundles to encourage cost-conscious travellers to convert. Since search engines display paid results before organic results — and even above some Featured Snippets in Google — this campaign put the Priceline listings first in Google Search. Despite its competitor Expedia spending $4.3 billion on PPC during the same time frame, Priceline reported positive results from this PPC campaign. 7. Hinge TikTok advertising The dating app Hinge created a social media campaign that endorsed deleting the app. While most apps want users to stay for as long as possible, Hinge promoted itself as “The dating app that’s meant to be deleted” — presumably when its users find love. This digital marketing strategy example is genius because of Hinge’s clever targeting. The app primarily targets Gen Z young adults looking for relationships. After some research, Hinge went to the place where its audience spends the most time — TikTok. Businesses are just starting to maximise TikTok ad performance and watch time, but this tongue-in-cheek content turned heads. The ad garnered millions of views on TikTok and more than 13 million views on YouTube. 8. Glossier social media strategy Makeup brand Glossier has a great example of a digital marketing strategy for social media. The brand knows how to leverage its large Instagram following of well over 2.7 million people. Glossier isn’t afraid to add personality to its social media content. In a clear break from most beauty brands, its photos aren’t typical, stlylised marketing. Instead, the photos show makeup and beauty products as they would look in a shopper’s home. Glossier’s social feed features everyday people in normal settings. Instead of relying on big-name influencers, it employs user-generated content to give its campaigns a sense of authenticity. The brand understands that its followers prefer to see realistic, everyday makeup and that’s exactly what Glossier offers with its social media marketing strategy. 9. Urban Outfitters SMS marketing and chatbot Few brands invest in SMS marketing, but it can be a crafty digital marketing strategy because users are surprisingly receptive to it. More than half of consumers reply to texts within two minutes and 70% have opted in to receive texts from businesses. Facing increased competition, fashion lifestyle brand Urban Outfitters created an SMS marketing campaign to deepen shopper relationships. Urban Outfitters already had an active email list, but it wasn’t sure whether contacting these same shoppers via SMS would hurt engagement levels. The brand conducted a split test and found that active email subscribers were equally active on SMS. This showed that the brand could do both SMS and email marketing to boost engagement even more. But Urban Outfitters doesn’t just market its brand via SMS — it also delivers customer service via text message. The UO Chatbot provides immediate customer support within a shopper’s SMS app. Customers can check their order status, view return policies and talk to a human customer service agent if the chatbot can’t help. At a time when companies are competing on customer service, investing in this digital marketing strategy helped Urban Outfitters stand out from other fashion brands. 10. Cosmic Crisp’s Hulu streaming ads Over-the-top ads are a new type of digital marketing strategy that’s gaining traction. As more consumers cancel cable and opt for streaming services like Hulu and Sling, brands are flocking to these spaces to continue engaging with viewers. That’s what the apple brand Cosmic Crisp did. In a bid to increase sales, the company paid for OTT ads on Hulu to feature its “ Slice Any Way ” video ad. The brand used Hulu Ad Manager to bid on ad spots, similar to how brands bid for PPC placements. Cosmic Crisp targeted foodies and parents with Hulu’s targeting options to reach thousands of streamers. Creating your digital marketing strategy Digital marketing is the future, but with so many strategies to choose from, it can feel overwhelming. Pull from these 10 high-profile examples of digital marketing strategies to build or improve your own tactics going forward. When you’re ready to get started, first decide which digital marketing channels work best for your business. Create a branded hashtag if you have a social media presence, revamp your newsletters if you have a large email list or choose another one of the strategies we’ve shared. text: Digital marketing strategies make your brand more visible on the internet. Today, most businesses invest in digital marketing, but often it’s without a concrete strategy that supports their goals. This dilutes results. This guide covers the types of digital marketing strategies and how to build one that draws in the right audience. What is a digital marketing strategy? A digital marketing strategy is a plan for how your business will grow visibility and capture your audience on digital channels like social media, the web, and AI platforms. “Audience” is the operative word here. Many brands try to follow the latest marketing trends in their industry, or use the latest tools, but forget to prioritize their audience. A digital marketing strategy that doesn’t center on your audience’s interests, pain points, and jobs-to-be-done won’t be effective. You might still get site traffic , likes, or followers. But this will come from the wrong audience, so conversions will suffer. A digital marketing strategy includes campaigns and tactics. Here’s how they’re different: Digital marketing strategy Digital marketing campaign Digital marketing tactic Long-term plan that supports business priorities. A targeted execution of a part of the strategy that supports a specific goal. It can span multiple channels. An action within a marketing campaign on a single channel. Digital marketing strategies are typically set quarterly or every six months, with monthly performance evaluation. Key components of a digital marketing strategy Your audience is the foundational component of your digital marketing strategy. Without understanding your ideal customer profile (ICP), it’s harder to select the right marketing channels, define goals, and determine your budget. Here’s how this and other components influence your digital marketing strategy: Audience: Who you’re targeting and what they care about. If your primary audience is startup marketers, then you need to understand their challenges and goals to target them. These could be a lack of budget, frequent pivots, wearing many hats at once, etc. Goals: The main outcome that all the marketing campaigns and tactics ladder up to. For example, the goal could be to increase product adoption by startup marketers by 20%. Channel: The ways you will reach your core audience. Your ICP also influences channel selection. For startup marketers, LinkedIn would be an important channel. Budget: How much you’re willing to spend per channel. Also consider whether your investment in each channel will bring compounding long-term results. Metric: What you will measure to evaluate if the strategy is working. Consider both leading and lagging indicators. Let's say your company offers a software platform that simplifies reporting for marketing teams. Your goal is to increase product signups by 20% in the next quarter. You could reach this audience on LinkedIn by promoting a webinar about automating weekly and monthly reporting. Then you'd track webinar sign-ups as a leading indicator and product signups as the lagging indicator. Why is a digital marketing strategy important? A digital marketing strategy is table stakes for both B2B and B2C businesses. Without it, you’re nearly invisible in digital channels that customers use to research and find products and services. Here are a few of the biggest benefits of digital marketing strategy planning: Clear direction and focus: Developing a strategy requires audience research, competitive analysis, and goal mapping. You’ll glean important insights to guide your work and prevent random acts of marketing. Marketing team success and accountability: Marketers are most successful when they have a strategy to execute. It also keeps them accountable for achieving specific goals. Better customer understanding: A digital marketing strategy helps you better understand your business’s target audience. This can lead to successful marketing campaigns that align with customers’ pain points, needs, and preferences. However, these benefits depend on marketers having access to customer data. HubSpot's 2026 research found that 12.4% of marketing leaders cite data sharing across teams as a barrier, and 19.5% struggle to adopt truly data-driven strategies. If you don’t know who your customers are and what challenges they face, you can run into major issues like using messaging that doesn’t resonate with customers. Or poorly targeted marketing campaigns. Types of digital marketing strategies The seven types below are the levers a digital marketing strategy pulls to reach your audience: SEO, agentic search optimization, content marketing, paid advertising, social media, email, and influencer marketing. They aren't a checklist to work through. They're choices you make based on where your audience spends time and what will move them to act. Each one uses a different mix of channels, your website, search engines, social platforms, email, and AI, to put your message in front of your ideal customer profile (ICP) when it matters. Search engine optimization (SEO) SEO is a strategy that improves your website’s visibility in Google and other search engines. Websites with good SEO rank higher in search results for their target keywords, deliver a good user experience, and build topical authority in their industry. The core pillars of SEO include: On-page SEO : Focuses on page and content structure Off-page SEO : Uses other authoritative websites to build your domain’s authority Technical SEO : Optimizes the website’s backend, including page speed and architecture Keyword research : Finds search terms you want to prioritize ranking for SEO is a foundational digital marketing strategy because its return compounds over time. Improve your site's speed or structure and Google is more likely to rank you higher, which puts your brand in front of more potential customers who can convert. SEO also underpins AI search: the same topical authority and content structure that earn rankings shape which sites AI platforms cite. So even as AI search grows, strong SEO does double duty, making you more competitive in traditional search and more visible in AI answers. Agentic search optimization Agentic search optimization (ASO) is the process of optimizing your digital presence for AI agents. In agentic search , AI agents answer user queries by autonomously browsing the internet, evaluating options, and then choosing the most relevant ones to present. ASO is an umbrella term that covers: Generative engine optimization (GEO) : How your brand appears in a model's training data and knowledge Answer engine optimization (AEO) : How AI tools process and cite your content in real time LLM optimization (LLMO) : Your presence and rankings within large language models ASO has been hard for marketers because there's so much conflicting advice and so many one-off tactics that don't add up to a complete strategy. That's why we built the Brand Orchestration Lifecycle as part of the Brand Visibility framework we unveiled at Adobe Summit. It's a four-stage system for approaching ASO methodically: Foundation : Create a clear brand narrative, define your entities, identify your audience, and find the topics you need to own Content : Publish multi-format content assets rooted in that foundation Distribution : Activate those assets across channels and surfaces Feedback : Use AI visibility signals like citations, sentiment, and rankings to refine your approach To see how you're showing up in AI search, Semrush's AI Visibility Toolkit benchmarks your brand's visibility across AI platforms and points you to where to focus next. Enter your domain and click “ Get started .” In the “Visibility Overview” dashboard, scroll down to “ What's Next? ” This carousel contains actionable strategies to boost your AI visibility, like topic identification and domain optimization. The “Brand Performance” dashboard provides a breakdown of your brand perception and share of voice compared to your rivals. You can use the AI-generated insights to get ideas for your ASO strategy. “Key Business Drivers” shows all the factors that support brand growth in your industry. And where each competitor is positioned in each driver. Use this data to inform how you talk about your brand and products on your website. For example, if you have low or no mentions in a specific business driver category, build a topic cluster for your content strategy where you will talk about it. Content marketing Content marketing is the use of written, visual, or audio content to capture your ICP. This type of digital marketing strategy focuses on education first, selling second. As part of your content marketing strategy, you can publish: Blog posts Podcasts YouTube tutorials Interviews with experts Case studies Whitepapers Webinars Newsletters A good content marketing strategy allows you to reach your audience when they’re trying to solve a problem. For example, if you target startup marketers, you could publish a blog post about how startups can build brand visibility on a lean budget. It speaks to a real pain point startup marketers have, and when the content is genuinely helpful and comprehensive, it positions you as an expert on the topic. When creating your content marketing strategy , take a multimodal approach to your blog content. This means including videos and images in articles to make them more engaging to your ICP. AI can also access multimodal content, so by including it on your website, you’re increasing the likelihood AI cites your page. Paid advertising Paid advertising promotes your brand using paid placements on digital platforms. It puts you in front of your audience immediately. Many brands use SEO and paid ads at the same time. SEO builds long-term, compounding visibility while paid campaigns enable short-term wins. But to maximize the likelihood of conversions, the ads still need hooks that speak to your audience and persuasive copy. Here are the main types of paid ads: Display advertising places ads on websites and apps Search engine advertising (SEM) uses sponsored placements in search results on Google, Bing, etc. Social media advertising reaches your audiences on platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and other channels A recent development in the paid advertising space is the emergence of ads on AI platforms. For example, ChatGPT has started rolling out ads in certain territories and introduced cost-per-click (CPC) bidding. Social media marketing Social media marketing is the process of building your visibility on social media platforms to attract your audience and build a connection with your brand. Also, social commerce features on platforms like Instagram and TikTok let people discover and buy products without leaving the app. Success on social media requires consistency, authenticity, and staying up to date with trends that drive user engagement. Keeping up with trends is one of the biggest challenges in social media marketing today, according to HubSpot's 2026 Social Media Marketing report . So you need to know exactly who you’re targeting on social media and what they care about. For example, skincare brand Paula’s Choice uses short clips on Instagram to discuss skin conditions and how its products help. The format — person holding a microphone and talking to the camera — is aligned with how many Instagram and TikTok creators produce educational video content for Gen Z and Millennial audiences. If you’re a small marketing team, prioritize the one or two platforms your audience uses most, rather than spreading yourself thin across many at once. For instance, B2B brands focus on LinkedIn, because decision-makers use it to follow industry conversations. Email marketing Email marketing targets your audience with promotional, transactional, and informative content. One advantage of email over other channels is that it isn't algorithm-driven. It's a direct line to your audience, and you can personalize your outreach to keep it relevant and helpful. The email marketing platforms most marketers use today allow you to set up audience segmentation and automation triggers. With segmentation, you can categorize subscribers by previous purchases, location, and any other unique characteristics. Then target them with personalized offers. Automation allows you to send personalized emails after a customer completes an action. Here’s an example using iHerb. The company sends an automated welcome email with a discount to new users who haven’t opted in to the newsletter yet. Your email marketing strategy can also benefit from AI personalization. For example, AI can automatically personalize subject lines, email openers, offers, and more to improve an email campaign’s performance. Influencer marketing Influencer marketing is the process of collaborating with social media creators who have a strong relationship with your audience. Influencer partnerships are a different lever compared to your owned channels because you're getting access to someone else's following. And in exchange, you pay influencers a flat fee, send gifts, or set up affiliate deals. The use of promo codes and affiliate links help you tie creator activity directly to sales, while engagement metrics allow you to measure overall campaign visibility. Collaborations include one-off sponsored posts, ongoing creator partnerships, or user-generated content (UGC) you can repurpose across your own channels. For example, software platform ServiceNow partnered with Instagram creator Corporate.bro to create a skit that promotes its new features. This creator has grown to over a million followers by publishing funny videos about working in corporate environments. So there’s a clear overlap between his and ServiceNow’s audience. Influencers are typically categorized based on their following: Nano-influencers: 1K-10K followers/subscribers Micro-influencers: 10K-100K followers/subscribers Mid-tier influencers: 100K-500K followers/subscribers Macro-influencers: 500K-1M followers/subscribers Mega-influencers: 1M+ followers/subscribers When evaluating influencers, go beyond followers and look at user engagement. Do their posts get views, comments, and shares? Influencers with smaller followings often have higher engagement rates. For example, an eMarketer study found nano-influencers have the highest Instagram engagement rate at 6.23%. Semrush’s Influencer Analytics tool helps you find the right influencers for your campaigns across social media platforms. You can filter them by audience size, views, pricing, or use the AI search tool to describe what kind of influencer you need. The tool also has a campaign management feature that lets you track the success of influencer collaborations. How to build a digital marketing strategy The seven steps below will help you create a digital marketing strategy: Step 1: Define your brand Defining your brand means getting clear on your brand identity and how it’s different from the competition. It’s the foundation of all marketing strategies. One of the key factors when creating your brand identity is identifying the emotions you want to evoke in your audience. For example, if you’re a B2B brand targeting enterprise clients, your brand should convey trust, security, and the ability to handle complexity. Cybersecurity platform WitnessAI does this with reassurance-driven messaging, positioning itself as a confidence layer that lets enterprises adopt AI without sacrificing security. Brand values are another core aspect of your identity: the beliefs and ideas your company represents. Visual elements like typography and colors are also important as they leave a lasting impression on your audience. When done well, they make your logo, digital ads, or billboards memorable. Step 2: Research your target audience Researching your target audience will help you choose the right digital marketing strategies for your brand. If you don’t understand your buyers, then you won’t know what they care about, the channels they use, or how they speak about their problems. And your strategy will fall flat. During audience research, you need to collect different types of data: Demographic data: Age, location, career, education Psychographic data: Interests, pain points, jobs-to-be-done, lifestyle habits Firmographic data (for B2B brands): Company size, industry, revenue, location Semrush's Traffic & Market Toolkit includes an Audience Profile section for researching any group of domains. Its Demographics dashboard shows audience insights like age, sex, and geographic distribution. The “Socioeconomics” dashboard dives deeper into data like household size, income level, and education of the audience of the brands you’re analyzing. You can also gather audience insights by doing interviews, joining online communities they participate in, or running surveys. Research reports by reputable industry sources are another great place to get started. Step 3: Analyze your competition Competitor analysis is a process that looks at your rivals’ brand positioning, market perception, and search and AI visibility. Here’s a breakdown of each: Brand positioning Market perception Search visibility AI visibility Analyze each competitor’s website to understand product positioning, value props, pricing, etc. Find customer reviews, check news publications, and dig into social media platforms to see how others talk about their solutions. Check if your competitors are visible in Google and other search engines, especially for non-branded search terms. Assess whether AI platforms cite and mention your competitors for key prompts. Semrush can help you measure search and AI visibility. First, paste your competitor’s domain into Organic Rankings , click “ Search ”, then go to “ Positions .” This tab shows all the keywords the competitor’s website ranks for in search, including branded and non-branded terms. Note the number of search positions, their search volume, and estimated traffic. To identify non-branded search terms a competitor ranks for, go to “ Advanced filters ” and set it to exclude keywords containing the company’s name. Go through the filtered list to find the competitor’s top rankings. Check if those keywords align with topics relevant to your audience. If yes, you should plan to capture those rankings if you haven’t already. Semrush's Competitor Research report , part of the AI Visibility Toolkit, finds the prompts where your rivals are visible but you aren't. Start by adding your domain and up to four competitors. Click “ Run competitor analysis .” The AI Visibility graph shows your visibility score relative to your competitors. To the right, “Competitor Insights” surfaces key topics where AI platforms mention your rivals with actionable tips. Scroll down to “Topics & Prompts” to get a closer look at the topics where your competitors are visible in AI search and how you compare. Click the arrow to expand the topic and see the performance for each prompt. Like with the previous step, find prompts that are highly relevant to your target audience and check if your brand shows up in AI responses. For more tips on growing your AI presence, check out our comprehensive guide to AI visibility . Step 4: Set SMART goals SMART goals stand for specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound objectives for your digital marketing strategy. Here’s an example of a SMART goal: “Increase AI referral traffic to the blog by 10% over the next six months by publishing 10 new articles per month and updating existing content.” This goal is: Specific (targeting an increase in AI referral traffic) Measurable (quantifying the target with a 10% increase) Achievable (possible to accomplish through consistent content creation and refreshes) Relevant (focused on improving the website’s AI reach) Time-bound (setting a deadline of six months to accomplish the goal) This way, the marketing team is clear on performance expectations and can align their activities accordingly. Step 5: Audit your existing content assets If you're not starting from scratch, audit your existing content to evaluate its performance, audience alignment, and improvement opportunities. Consider both the content on your website and third-party platforms like YouTube. When going through your content assets, put yourself in your audience’s shoes and ask if they’d consider the content helpful. Any assets that target the wrong personas or are no longer relevant to your brand are candidates for content pruning . This is especially important for AI visibility. For example, you might have outdated content on your website that targets startup founders. But if your company has pivoted to enterprise buyers, an AI platform could still cite the old content and position you incorrectly. Follow our seven-step content audit process (with free template included) to get started. Step 6: Choose your channels and allocate budget Your choice of marketing channels depends on your audience, goals, budget, market position, and the size of your marketing team. Here are two examples using hypothetical companies. Fast-growing B2C startup A B2C series A startup with a one-person marketing team is under pressure to capture customers in a saturated market. They have a considerable budget but also need to show ROI quickly. The startup builds a digital marketing strategy that focuses on paid ads, blogs targeting commercial keywords , and influencer partnerships. The paid ads and commercial blog content drive new users with 60% budget allocation, while influencer partnerships help them reach a new audience. B2B SaaS company A software company needs to build brand awareness. They only work with large organizations and sign contracts worth millions of dollars. They rely on their sales team to generate revenue, but need marketing to build trust and visibility. The company’s digital marketing strategy focuses entirely on content: insightful research reports and blogs. The sales team distributes the research reports with prospects, while the blogs get traffic from buyers who want to learn more about the latest trends and solutions in their industry. Step 7: Measure, optimize, and iterate To measure the success of your digital marketing strategy, you need analytics tools to collect user data. This includes tools like: Google Analytics for website and/or app traffic Semrush for search and AI visibility tracking Semrush Social Toolkit for social media scheduling and analytics ActiveCampaign for email analytics You also need to set up conversion tracking on your website so you can see which pages and channels drive the most revenue. Get the conversion tracking in place before launching your marketing strategy to avoid missing important data. Once the data starts rolling in, combine the insights from each tool into a cohesive story. For instance, a blog post might have a 10% signup rate from organic channels despite low overall traffic. You could pull data from Semrush and Google Search Console to see the keywords it ranks for, their search volumes, and if any indicate high purchasing intent. To optimize your digital marketing strategy for better results, run A/B tests and analyze the performance data on a monthly basis. Use the insights to iterate on new campaigns, taking note of any hooks, formats, or topics that perform better than others. How digital marketing channels work together Using multiple digital marketing channels creates a cycle where visibility on one channel strengthens performance on another. Marketing channels are grouped into the following categories: Owned channels : Owned by your company. Include websites, email, social media profiles, etc. Earned or shared channels : Belong to a third party that promotes your brand Paid channels : You pay to promote your content. Includes ads on social media, search engines, music streaming platforms, etc. Here’s an example of how they work together. SEO builds your website's topical authority and drives organic traffic from search and AI platforms. Once on your website, a percentage of visitors sign up for your email list, which gives you a direct way to nurture them toward a purchase. At the same time, paid ads bring in new, high-intent visitors who may not have found you organically yet. Social media allows you to reach a wider audience and build brand recognition. This has a downstream effect on search because people who've seen your brand on social are more likely to click your result in Google, which improves your organic click-through rate. Digital marketing strategy example: The Ordinary The Ordinary's digital marketing strategy is built on ingredient transparency. It’s aimed at skincare enthusiasts who research products, understand formulations, and prioritize quality and efficacy over brand names or marketing hype. Every channel reinforces this message. The brand's blog publishes content that covers formulations, skincare tips, and ingredients. This helps capture new customers who are beginning to research these concepts. On social media, The Ordinary posts about product launches, campaigns, and skincare advice. Much of the skincare advice takes a myth-busting approach, and exposes common misconceptions: The brand also uses influencer partnerships to spread the word about new products. For example, creator HydrationCEO published a reel walking viewers through The Ordinary's reformulated hyaluronic acid. Continually refine your digital marketing strategy Marketing teams are busier than ever, because AI lets them do more on every channel, from blogs to videos to paid campaigns, and the pressure to show results is high. A positive side to this is you have more data to work with. You can see quickly which pages convert better or which topics drive more traffic to your site. Use the insights to refine your digital marketing strategy monthly, and revisit the approach quarterly.
